metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with a deployable entry point (@WebService JAX-WS annotation on PurchaseOrderService.java) and a WSDL contract present. Single service with database access via JDBC.
metadata.archetype_justification: The service performs database writes (INSERT INTO partner_orders) via JDBC, owns persistent state in Oracle 11g, and exposes a SOAP endpoint for partner order submission.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.22 yields Not Ready band but 11 High findings (below >=12 threshold) resolves to Remediation Required tier. Divergence arises because 20 non-core questions score 1 (Medium severity, not High), keeping High count at 11 while dragging overall numeric score below 1.5. The count-based tier (Remediation Required) is authoritative per the classification table.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: Given the extreme simplicity of this service (single operation, single table, ~50 lines of logic), a full Strangler Fig migration is recommended. Build a new modern service alongside the SOAP endpoint while migrating partners incrementally.

approaches.name: Strengthen as Modular Monolith
approaches.applicability: Not applicable — the service is already minimal; there are no modules to strengthen.

approaches.name: Strangler Fig (Parallel Track)
approaches.applicability: Build a new modern service (REST/event-driven) alongside the SOAP endpoint. Route new partners to the new API; migrate existing partners incrementally.

approaches.name: Conditional / Adaptive
approaches.applicability: Containerize first then rewrite. However, JBoss 5.1/Java 6 is too obsolete to containerize without major rework.

approaches.name: Big-Bang Rewrite
approaches.applicability: Acceptable given minimal scope — but frame as new service not rewrite.

decomposition_strategy.effort_estimate: Medium (3-6 months total including partner migration)

findings.title: No managed compute — JBoss AS 5.1 on RHEL 6
findings.description: All compute runs on JBoss AS 5.1 deployed on RHEL 6 with Java 6. Both the application server and operating system are past end-of-life. No managed container orchestration, no serverless, no Fargate.
findings.gap: No managed compute services in use. The entire stack is self-managed and EOL.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed compute: containerize on ECS/Fargate or rewrite as a Lambda function behind API Gateway. Requires upgrading from Java 6 to Java 17+ and from JBoss to a modern runtime first.

findings.title: Self-managed Oracle 11g database
findings.description: Oracle 11g accessed via direct JDBC to jdbc:oracle:thin:@10.0.9.30:1521:PARTDB. The database is self-managed with no managed database services in use.
findings.gap: Database is entirely self-managed with no automated failover, no managed backups, and no scaling capabilities. Oracle 11g is past EOL.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL. The schema is simple (single table) with no stored procedures, making engine migration straightforward via AWS DMS and SCT.

findings.title: No workflow orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. The single operation is entirely hardcoded in a single method. For the stateful-crud archetype, all workflow logic is hardcoded in application code.
findings.gap: No dedicated workflow orchestration. All logic is in a single method with no structure for multi-step operations.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, implement AWS Step Functions for any multi-step order processing workflows.

findings.title: No async messaging or streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. Partner order submissions are synchronous SOAP calls that block until the database insert completes. For the stateful-crud archetype, there is no messaging where state changes cross service boundaries.
findings.gap: No async messaging for cross-service communication. Order events are not propagated to other systems.
findings.recommendation: Implement managed messaging (SQS/SNS or EventBridge) to decouple order submission from downstream processing.

findings.title: No network security configuration
findings.description: No network security configuration exists in the repository. No VPC, security groups, NACLs, or network segmentation. Service exposed over plain HTTP.
findings.gap: No IaC-defined network security. Service exposed over plain HTTP with no verifiable network isolation.
findings.recommendation: Define network infrastructure in IaC: VPC with private subnets, least-privilege security groups, TLS termination at ALB or API Gateway.

findings.title: No API entry point or load balancer
findings.description: SOAP service exposed directly on port 8080 with no API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront. No throttling, no authentication at the entry point.
findings.gap: No managed entry point — service directly exposed with no traffic management.
findings.recommendation: Deploy behind API Gateway (for REST migration) or ALB with WAF for throttling, authentication, and request validation.

findings.title: No auto-scaling configured
findings.description: No auto-scaling configuration exists. The service runs on a single JBoss instance with static capacity.
findings.gap: All capacity is statically provisioned with no ability to scale with demand.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling when migrating to managed compute: ECS service auto-scaling or Lambda concurrency limits.

findings.title: No backup and recovery configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration found. The Oracle 11g database has no visible backup plan, no PITR, no retention policy.
findings.gap: No automated backup configuration. Recovery procedures are undocumented.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to RDS/Aurora, enable automated backups with >=7-day retention and PITR. Document and test restore procedures.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code coverage
findings.description: 0% IaC coverage. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any IaC artifacts exist. All infrastructure is manually created.
findings.gap: No Infrastructure as Code — all infrastructure is manual (ClickOps). Blocks reproducible deployments and disaster recovery.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in IaC (Terraform or CDK): compute, networking, database, monitoring, and operational resources.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Builds use Ant with wsgen/wsimport run by hand. Deployments are entirely manual.
findings.gap: No CI/CD automation — all builds and deployments are manual.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild): build, test, SAST scan, deploy to staging, integration test, deploy to production.

findings.title: Compound legacy Java 6 with JAX-WS
findings.description: Java 6 with JAX-WS (javax.jws) framework. No Spring Boot, no modern framework, no AWS SDK. Language version, framework, and SDK all regressed.
findings.gap: Java 6 is past EOL. JAX-WS RPC/encoded is deprecated. No modern cloud-native framework or AWS SDK.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Java 17+ with Spring Boot 3.x (or Quarkus) and AWS SDK v2.

findings.title: Tightly-coupled single-class monolith
findings.description: Single-class monolith with all logic in one method. No module boundaries, no separation of concerns. XML parsing, database access, and error handling all interleaved.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries and pervasive shared state.
findings.recommendation: Decompose into a properly structured service with separation of concerns. See Decomposition Strategy section.

findings.title: All communication synchronous with no async patterns
findings.description: All communication is synchronous SOAP over HTTP. For the stateful-crud archetype, this scores 1: all communication synchronous HTTP with no async patterns.
findings.gap: 100% synchronous communication. State changes are not propagated asynchronously.
findings.recommendation: Implement async patterns for cross-service state propagation: emit order events to SQS/SNS/EventBridge after persistence.

findings.title: No async job handling for long-running operations
findings.description: All operations are synchronous regardless of duration. For the stateful-crud archetype, there is no infrastructure for handling long-running operations.
findings.gap: No async job infrastructure. All operations synchronous with no mechanism for long-running processes.
findings.recommendation: Implement async job handling: SQS + Lambda workers or Step Functions for batch processing with status polling endpoints.

findings.title: No API versioning strategy
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. WSDL namespace contains no version identifier. No URL patterns, no version headers.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly to all consumers.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL path versioning (/v1/orders) for the modernized REST API. Maintain legacy SOAP endpoint during migration.

findings.title: Hard-coded service endpoint with no discovery
findings.description: Service endpoint hard-coded in WSDL: http://partner-svc.acme-corp.internal:8080/po/PurchaseOrderService. No service discovery, no API catalog.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hard-coded — no dynamic discovery.
findings.recommendation: Implement service discovery via API Gateway or AWS Cloud Map.

findings.title: No managed object storage for unstructured data
findings.description: Partner purchase orders submitted as raw XML are parsed in-memory. Original XML documents are not stored. No S3, no document storage, no parsing pipeline.
findings.gap: Unstructured data (purchase order XML) processed transiently with no persistent object storage. Original documents lost.
findings.recommendation: Store original purchase order XML in S3 with lifecycle policies. Implement parsing pipeline for structured extraction.

findings.title: No unified data access layer
findings.description: Database access performed directly in service method via raw JDBC with string-concatenated SQL. No DAO pattern, no repository layer, no ORM, no connection pooling.
findings.gap: No data access layer — database queries scattered in business logic with raw JDBC.
findings.recommendation: Implement a unified data access layer using Spring Data JPA or repository pattern.

findings.title: Database engine past end-of-life
findings.description: Oracle 11g in use — reached end of Extended Support in 2022. No version pinning in IaC (no IaC exists). Engine is past EOL.
findings.gap: Database engine past end-of-life. No version management or upgrade procedure.
findings.recommendation: Migrate from Oracle 11g to Amazon RDS PostgreSQL or Aurora PostgreSQL via AWS DMS.

findings.title: No encryption at rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configuration. Oracle database accessed via plain JDBC with no TLS/SSL. No KMS keys, no encryption configuration.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest configured for the data store.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to RDS/Aurora, enable encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS key. Enable TLS for database connections.

findings.title: Static credential authentication over plaintext HTTP
findings.description: WS-Security username token authentication with passwords in plaintext over HTTP. Static credential authentication without modern token-based auth.
findings.gap: Static credential authentication (WS-Security PasswordText) over plain HTTP. No token-based auth.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to OAuth2/JWT-based authentication with API Gateway and Cognito authorizer. Enforce TLS.

findings.title: No centralized identity integration
findings.description: No centralized identity provider integration. Partner credentials stored in a flat properties file. Application manages authentication independently.
findings.gap: Application manages its own authentication with no external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito. Create User Pool for partner credentials with MFA.

findings.title: Hardcoded database credentials in source code
findings.description: Database credentials hardcoded directly in source: DB_USER = 'partner_app', DB_PASS = 'partner2009'. Plaintext credentials committed to version control.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code — critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Immediately remove hardcoded credentials. Store all secrets in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: No compute hardening or patching strategy
findings.description: No compute hardening or patching. JBoss AS 5.1 and RHEL 6 are past EOL with known unpatched vulnerabilities.
findings.gap: No patching strategy. Runtime stack is EOL with no security updates.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed compute with hardened base images (Bottlerocket for containers, AWS-managed Lambda runtimes). Enable ECR image scanning.

findings.title: No application security pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No CI/CD pipeline to integrate SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. Known vulnerabilities (XXE, SQL injection) exist undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning — vulnerabilities remain undetected.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (SonarQube/Semgrep), dependency scanning (Dependabot/Snyk), and container scanning into CI/CD with security gates.

findings.title: No distributed tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing instrumented. No OpenTelemetry SDK, no X-Ray, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing — request flows are invisible.
findings.recommendation: Instrument the modernized service with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency thresholds, no error budget tracking.
findings.gap: No formal SLO definitions or monitoring — service levels are unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs: order submission latency p99 < 500ms, availability > 99.9%, error rate < 0.1%.

findings.title: No business metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business event tracking, no dashboards.
findings.gap: No business metrics — only infrastructure metrics available.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics: orders per partner, amounts, success/failure rates, processing latency.

findings.title: No anomaly detection or alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Failures only visible when partners report them.
findings.gap: No alerting — failures go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms with anomaly detection on error rates and latency. Integrate with incident management tool.

findings.title: No automated tests of any kind
findings.description: No automated tests. No unit tests, no integration tests, no contract tests. Partner onboarding is a manual SOAP-UI session.
findings.gap: Zero automated tests — all validation is manual. Regression risk is extreme.
findings.recommendation: Create integration test suite: contract tests, database integration tests, end-to-end order submission tests. Run in CI pipeline.

findings.title: No observability ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS for monitoring, no per-service dashboards, no alarm ownership.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring is absent entirely.
findings.recommendation: Define observability ownership: per-service dashboards, alarm ownership, SLO accountability.
